children: Berkshire Hathaway posted a 28% decline in quarterly net income after investment gains slumped and the conglomerate's insurance operations reported lower profits.
The Omaha, Neb.-based company continued to put more of its massive cash trove to work, repurchasing more of its own shares during the quarter.

Berkshire ended the third quarter with around $357 billion in cash and Treasury bills after accounting for a payable for purchasing some of the short-term government debt, a 2.1% decrease from three months earlier and the second-straight sequential drop.

The quarter also marked the end of Warren Buffett's long run as Berkshire's chairman. Buffett, 96, ceded the post to his son Howard Buffett in September. Greg Abel succeeded Buffett as CEO in January.
Net income fell to $22.11 billion, or $15,502 per Class A share, from $30.8 billion, or $21,413 a share, a year earlier.
The S&P 500 rose 2% during the third quarter, when U.S. Treasury yields surged.

Operating earnings, which exclude some investment results, slipped 5.8% to $12.71 billion from $13.49 billion. Profits from Berkshire's insurance-underwriting business fell sharply from a year ago, when the company benefited from a mild hurricane season and a turnaround from its auto insurer, Geico.
Berkshire's railroad and energy businesses reported higher profits, as did its portfolio of manufacturing, service and retailing companies.

Buffett has said that operating earnings are the better measure of the company's performance. Accounting rules require Berkshire to include unrealized gains and losses from its giant investment portfolio when it reports net income, meaning that short-term fluctuations in the stock market can cause big swings in quarterly income.
The company repurchased 4,536 Class A shares and 12,384,959 Class B shares during the third quarter, for around $9.6 billion.

Berkshire bought $2.4 billion of stocks during the September quarter and sold some $2.82.8 billion in the same period. Berkshire's largest holdings are Alphabet, American Express, Apple, Bank of America and Coca-Cola. The company is set to disclose more specifics on its stock portfolio in a regulatory filing later this month.
Berkshire's Class A shares are up more than 13% this year, and closed at a record high of around $869,301 on Wednesday.

The stock had previously been on a tumble after closing at a new high in May 2025, the day before Warren Buffett announced his retirement from the CEO post. But Berkshire rallied for much of October, as tech stocks began to slump amid fears over the AI build-out.
